newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. hopes to approve Iraqi food plan by week's end.
newsitem.headline: U.N. hopes to approve Iraqi food plan by week's end.

text.p: The United Nations is optimistic that its review of Iraq's food distribution plan under the "oil-for-food" programme can be completed by the end of the week, clearing the way for Secretary-General Kofi Annan to give his approval, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhart said on Tuesday.
He said Iraq's U.N. mission submitted more than 600 pages of annexes to the distribution plan on Monday.

"We are still optimistic that the secretariat's review of the entire package can be completed by the end of this week and that the secretary-general can then give his approval of the plan," Eckhard said.

Under the "oil-for-food" arrangement, which first took effect last Dec. 10, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and other necessities to help offset the effects of sanctions in place since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The programme was renewed for a second six-month period beginning on June 8, but Iraq has not so far sold any more oil pending United Nations approval of its latest food distribution plan.

Iraq had been hoping the latest six-month period would not start until its distribution plan had been cleared by the United Nations, but the Security Council insists the clock began ticking on June 8.
This means Iraq has only until Sept. 5 to sell the first $1 billion worth of oil allowed during each 90-day period.
